description.summary: private channel between the compositor and the Xwayland window manager helper

protocol.description:
This private protocol lets the compositor drive the X11 window manager helper (xw-xwm, a separate session process that speaks the X protocol on the compositor's behalf). The compositor deliberately contains no X11 code; geometry and close requests that would normally go through an embedded XWM are forwarded over this channel instead.
Windows are identified by the xwayland_shell_v1 serial (the same 64-bit value Xwayland sends both to the compositor via xwayland_surface_v1.set_serial and to the WM via the WL_SURFACE_SERIAL X client message), which both sides can correlate without any further state sharing.
The intended client of this protocol is the session's xw-xwm helper. Other clients may bind it; they gain no privileged ability (geometry and close flow one way, compositor to WM).

interface.name: xw_window_control_manager_v1

description.summary: window control events for the X WM helper

interface.description:
The compositor emits these events whenever an Xwayland-managed window changes geometry or focus, or is asked to close. The helper mirrors the geometry onto the X11 window (keeping X input coordinates aligned with the compositor placement), mirrors compositor keyboard focus into the X input focus, and performs the actual X11 close (WM_DELETE_WINDOW, else destroy).
Version 2 adds the reverse direction: the helper reports window identity (WM_NAME / WM_CLASS), override-redirect state and ICCCM size hints for windows it associates with a serial, so X11 windows become first-class citizens of the one compositor window model (taskbar titles, popup placement, resize constraints). Version 1 helpers never send the new requests and never receive the focus event.

event.name: geometry

description.summary: an Xwayland window moved or resized

event.description: The window identified by serial_hi/serial_lo is now at x,y with size width,height in compositor layout coordinates. Emitted at map time, after interactive move/resize, and on maximize, unmaximize, fullscreen, tile and similar geometry changes.

arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the xwayland surface serial

arg.name: serial_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the xwayland surface serial

arg.summary: new x position (layout coordinates)

arg.summary: new y position (layout coordinates)

arg.name: width

arg.name: height
arg.summary: new height

event.name: close

description.summary: the window was asked to close

event.description: The compositor already unmapped the window; the helper should now deliver WM_DELETE_WINDOW (or destroy the window) on the X side so the client actually terminates.

arg.name: serial_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the xwayland surface serial

arg.name: serial_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the xwayland surface serial

event.name: focus

description.summary: compositor keyboard focus moved to an X window

event.description: The compositor's keyboard focus is now the window with the given serial; the helper must route the X input focus accordingly (SetInputFocus and/or a WM_TAKE_FOCUS ClientMessage, per the window's ICCCM input model). A serial of 0 means no X11 window holds compositor focus (a native window, or none) and the X input focus should be released.

request.name: set_title
request.description: The window's WM_NAME (STRING) or _NET_WM_NAME (UTF8_STRING, preferred when present) as the X WM helper read it. Sent when the serial is first associated and again whenever the property changes (xterm and every terminal retitle themselves).

request.name: set_app_id
request.description: The res_class field of WM_CLASS — the same identity level the xdg-shell app_id carries for native windows, and what taskbars match rules and icons against.

arg.name: serial_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the xwayland surface serial

arg.name: serial_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the xwayland surface serial

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: WM_CLASS res_class

request.name: set_override_redirect
request.description: The X11 window behind this serial has override-redirect set (menus, tooltips, combo dropdowns). It is not a managed toplevel: the compositor must place it at exactly the given X11 geometry (the X client owns the position), keep it above all managed windows, and exclude it from the taskbar, focus and workspace switching. Re-sent whenever the window's X11 geometry changes.

request.name: set_size_hints
request.description: The window's WM_NORMAL_HINTS size constraints (0 = unset). The compositor applies them to interactive and programmatic resizes of this window, exactly as xdg-shell min/max sizes are applied to native windows; the helper additionally rounds client-initiated ConfigureRequest sizes itself.

request.name: set_geometry

description.summary: the X-side truth geometry of a managed window

request.description: The helper reports the window's geometry in compositor layout coordinates — the wl_surface extent (X11 interior size plus border) — after it granted a client-initiated resize (ConfigureRequest). The compositor adopts it as the window's geometry so its model matches X reality even when the client draws nothing after resizing: Xwayland only pushes a new surface buffer on damage, so an undrawn resize is invisible to the buffer-commit path. The compositor must not echo this back through the geometry event — the X side already has this state, and the helper's loop guard would drop a redundant configure anyway.
